title: Adaptive preemption lanes with staged-hosted spillover throttles and variant-priority sequencing
creator: Ben Morales
description:
Problem: During sustained load spikes tenants pinned to Dedicated capacity either starve or experience abrupt cutovers to Hosted with poor latency and model-quality regressions. Current spillover behavior is binary and stateless: when Dedicated is full, requests go to Hosted with a simple fallback model mapping. This causes customer-visible QoS cliffs, billing surprises, and undifferentiated model demotions.

Goal: Implement an adaptive routing tier that: (1) reserves short-lived preemption lanes on Dedicated for high-SLA tenants, (2) stages spillover to Hosted with throttles and progressive variant demotion (not immediate demotion to lowest-cost variant), and (3) exposes controls for tenants and platform operators to tune grace windows, backoff and rollback behavior. The feature should prioritize reliability (SLOs) while limiting unexpected cost and model-quality regressions.

Scope: Routing adjudicator + capacity scanner changes, policy config schema, tenant-level soft-commit tokens, progressive variant-priority sequencing, telemetry & dashboard updates, and rollout path (feature flag + canary). Not in scope: wholesale quota/ billing redesign (follow-up), deep model re-evaluation pipeline (handled by Optimize team).
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine accepts new policy schema 'adaptive_preemption' and returns deterministic routing decisions for simulated load traces
Dedicated preemption lanes allocated per-tenant for up to X seconds configurable (default 30s), configurable by admin and tenant-level override
Spillover to Hosted occurs through staged throttles: soft spill -> partial throttle -> full spillover. No sudden RTT cliffs in 95th percentile during canary
Variant-priority sequencing demotes model variants incrementally (primary -> warm-variant -> cold-variant) with per-stage rollback if latency or quality thresholds breach
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant preemption hits, staged spill stages, variant demotion counts, and cost delta estimates in Console
End-to-end tests (unit + integration + load) added and passing in CI; canary run for one region for 48 hours with synthetic traffic to validate behavior
Security review completed and approved for routing adjudicator changes
Documentation (Console UI knobs + API config examples) published and linked from PRD
